rows.selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so the main uncertainty is the baseline performance of a simple unimodal model. This tests a minimal RNA-only, single-profile PCA configuration to establish a validation accuracy/F1 reference point. It is the best first experiment because it is simple, avoids confounding effects from multiprofile aggregation, image encoders, or fusion, and provides a necessary anchor for later comparisons.

The only completed result is a weak RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline, so it is unclear whether image features contain useful signal. config_010 tests a simple image-only single-profile ResNet50 baseline, clarifying whether the image modality is competitive before investing in multimodal fusion or more complex aggregation. This is the best next use of budget because it reduces uncertainty about a major design decision with a simple, interpretable comparison rather than changing multiple factors at once.

RNA-only PCA singleprofile is currently the strongest result (0.485 accuracy, 0.464 F1), while image-only ResNet is weak (0.208 accuracy). The key uncertainty is whether multiple profiles plus simple aggregation can improve the promising RNA representation. config_002 keeps the same RNA encoder and changes only the profile/aggregation setting, making it a clean, low-risk extension of the current best direction. It is more informative than jumping to multimodal or new encoders because it tests whether profile aggregation is worth further investment.

RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool is the current best configuration, showing a clear improvement over singleprofile PCA and much stronger performance than image-only ResNet. This experiment tests whether transformer aggregation improves on avgpool for the same multiprofile PCA representation, isolating the effect of aggregation. It is the best next step because it exploits the strongest existing evidence with a minimal change, reducing uncertainty about profile aggregation before introducing new RNA encoders or multimodal fusion.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA-only PCA with multiprofile avgpool is the best configuration (0.591 accuracy, 0.573 F1), clearly above singleprofile PCA and multiprofile transformer aggregation, while image-only ResNet is weak. This suggests the promising direction is multiprofile avgpool RNA modeling, but the RNA representation choice remains untested beyond PCA. config_008 keeps the proven multiprofile avgpool setting and changes only the RNA encoder to scgpt, directly testing whether a stronger learned RNA representation improves on PCA. This is a single-factor extension of the current best configuration, has high expected value if scgpt helps, and clarifies whether representation is the main remaining RNA lever before investing in multimodal fusion.

The strongest evidence so far is that RNA multiprofile PCA with avgpool is the best configuration (accuracy 0.5907, F1 0.5727), outperforming singleprofile RNA and transformer aggregation, while image-only ResNet50 singleprofile is weak. The main uncertainty is whether image features can add value on top of the strongest RNA baseline. config_018 keeps the best RNA profile and aggregation setting and adds ResNet50 image features with simple concat fusion, directly testing the marginal benefit of multimodality under the strongest known RNA configuration. This is the best use of the next experiment because it exploits the strongest evidence, uses a simple fusion baseline to avoid confounding complexity, and will clarify whether further multimodal exploration is worthwhile.

The current best result is config_018 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) with 0.6186 accuracy and 0.6103 F1, modestly above the best RNA-only multiprofile avgpool PCA result (0.5907/0.5727). Because only concat fusion has been tested and the image-only ResNet50 result was weak, it is unclear whether simple concatenation is already sufficient or whether weighted fusion can better balance the modalities. config_019 changes only the fusion method from concat to weighted, keeping the otherwise promising setup fixed. This is the most efficient next experiment because it directly exploits the current best direction while isolating the effect of fusion, which can either improve performance or clarify that concat is adequate before exploring larger changes.

The strongest evidence so far is that multiprofile PCA RNA with avgpool aggregation and weighted multimodal fusion using ResNet50 gives the best validation accuracy and F1, while image-only ResNet50 is weak and ViT is untested. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l improves the current best multimodal setup while keeping profile setting, RNA encoder, aggregation, and fusion fixed. It is the best next use of budget because it exploits the most promising configuration, isolates the effect of image representation, and clarifies whether the current gain comes from fusion generally or from a stronger visual encoder.

The strongest evidence so far is for multimodal, multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion, PCA RNA, and ResNet-50 (config_019), with only small differences from ViT (config_025) and concat fusion (config_018). RNA-only results also suggest avgpool is safer than transformer and that PCA is currently the best tested RNA encoder, but scVI remains untested. config_031 keeps the current best pipeline and changes only the RNA encoder to scVI_n200, isolating the effect of RNA representation. This is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising setting while reducing uncertainty about whether a learned RNA encoder can improve over PCA/scGPT without introducing multiple confounding changes.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile avgpool and weighted multimodal fusion are strong, and scvi_n200 gives the best result so far (0.678 accuracy, 0.646 F1) with resnet50, but that is a single multimodal data point and the RNA encoder effect is confounded with fusion. config_005 tests scvi_n200 in the same RNA-only multiprofile avgpool setting as config_002 (pca_n2000, 0.591 accuracy) and config_008 (scgpt, 0.530 accuracy), changing only the RNA encoder. This will clarify whether the learned scvi representation is intrinsically better or mainly beneficial in multimodal fusion, and whether a simpler RNA-only model may be competitive. Under limited budget, this one-factor ablation efficiently reduces uncertainty about an important representation choice before committing further experiments to more complex multimodal extensions.
